name: name-constraints-explicit-minimum-zero-valid
description: permittedSubtrees contains a single GeneralSubtree for dNSName 'example.com' with the optional 'minimum' field encoded explicitly as INTEGER 0. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 says minimum 'MUST be zero' (and is OPTIONAL with default 0); DER would normally omit the field entirely because the default value is in effect. Some real CA software encodes the zero explicitly, producing a technically non-canonical-DER but RFC-compliant constraint. The leaf's SAN 'www.example.com' is inside the permitted subtree; the cert must be accepted.
references: OpenSSL c23e497da7 — accept explicit minimum=0 while still rejecting non-zero minimum and any maximum
notes: Companion to name-constraints-minimum-nonzero-invalid (which sets minimum=1 and expects rejection). This case tests the boundary where the field is present but carries the default value — strict DER-canonicality parsers may reject the cert at parse time, while implementations following OpenSSL's interop fix accept it.

ascii2der payload constructs SEQUENCE { [0] { SEQUENCE { SEQUENCE { [2 PRIMITIVE] { "example.com" } [0 PRIMITIVE] { `00` } } } } } — note the [0 PRIMITIVE] { 00 } encoding the BaseDistance minimum=0 explicitly.
